To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the NRIG model performs slightly better than other models, and the asymmetric GARCH model with NRIG distribution is a useful tool for risk management in the Hong Kong stock markets.

The asymmetric GARCH models with fat-tailed distribution (the Student’s t distribution, the normal inverse Gaussian (NIG) distribution and the new type of fat- tailed distribution, the NRIG distribution) are more suitable than the GARCH models with normal distribution for the risk management of Hong Kong stock market.
the GARCH-NRIG model outperforms other GARCH models in the risk management of Hong Kong stock market, and the introduction of GJR-terms improves the models’ performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new GARCH models for financial risk management.
the development of a new type of GARCH model that is more appropriate for the Hong Kong stock returns.
the empirical analysis of the Hong Kong market returns, and the findings can be used to improve the risk management practices of the industry participants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NRIG-GJR model outperforms the GARCH-t and NIG-GJR models in terms of both in-sample and out-of-sample performance.
the GARCH-NRIG model performs best in capturing the dynamics of the Hong Kong market returns.
the asymmetric GJR-NGARCH NRIG model is superior to other GARCH models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the asymmetric GJR-GARCH model with the normal reciprocal inverse gaussian distribution (GJR-NRIG) is a good candidate to model the conditional volatility of the Hong Kong Stock market returns, especially for the period of 1998-2008.
the GARCH models with fat-tailed distributions are very useful for the Hong Kong stock returns.
the asymmetric GJR-GARCH-NRIG model is the best model in terms of the goodness-of-fit and forecasting accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the asymmetric GJR-NRIG model provides the best fit to the Hong Kong stock returns, which is superior to other models considered in the paper.
the asymmetric GJR-terms should be included in the GARCH models, which can help practitioners to improve their risk management strategies.
the GARCH models with the NRIG distribution can provide a better fit to the data and a better forecast of volatility than the GARCH models using other types of distributions.
